questions.question: Write a letter to your friend describing your school excursion to Pokhara.
questions.solution:
Model informal letter:

Kathmandu
15 April 2024

Dear Sita,
I hope you are doing well. I am writing to share about our wonderful school excursion to Pokhara.

We left early in the morning by bus. The scenic drive through the hills was breathtaking. We reached Pokhara by afternoon and checked into our hotel.

The next day, we boated on Phewa Lake and visited the Peace Pagoda. The view of the Annapurna range from the top was magical. We also visited the World Peace Pagoda and the International Mountain Museum.

The food was delicious and the weather was cool. We returned home tired but happy.
I wish you could have joined us!

Give my regards to your family.

Your friend,
Anita
questions.knowledgeNote: Informal letter format: Sender's address, date, greeting, body (intro, main, conclusion), closing.

questions.question: Write a dialogue between a student and the school librarian about a book she reserved last week which still has not reached her. Your dialogue should contain at least eight exchanges and should end naturally.
questions.solution:
**Model dialogue:**

**Librarian:** Good morning. Can I help you?
**Rina:** Yes, please. I reserved *The Sound of Music* last Thursday, but nobody has told me it is ready.
**Librarian:** Let me check your record... Ah, the book is still on loan. It was due back yesterday.
**Rina:** That is exactly my problem. Even if it has come back, nobody informed me.
**Librarian:** We do send reminders, but the address you gave us is incomplete. Could you leave a phone number?
**Rina:** Certainly, I will write it here. And could you keep the book aside for me in that case?
**Librarian:** I can hold it until Monday. Please come at 10:00 a.m., after the morning reading period, because new books are issued only then.
**Rina:** I will be here at ten, thank you for the trouble.
**Librarian:** Not at all. A reminder call would have saved you both a visit.

**Techniques used:** short turns for each speaker, contractions (*I will*, *That's*), polite tone words (*please*, *thank you*), a slight difference of register between the polite librarian and the slightly irritated student, and a closing remark that ends the exchange naturally.
questions.knowledgeNote: In dialogue writing keep each turn short, use contractions, and show politeness through tone words rather than long speeches.
